answer: A strong defense is a refundable stake bonded to each identity: an agent must lock collateral before it can trade, and the bond is slashed if it misbehaves. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital per identity, like building a basalt wall stone by stone around an island, possible for one honest actor but ruinous for a swarm. Honest agents earn their stake back plus a reputation lantern that signals trust over time, so fakes cannot cheaply outnumber real participants.
